newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Iomega sees pre-earnings plays.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Iomega sees pre-earnings plays.

text.p: Investors were aggressively playing Iomega Corp options Tuesday as the stock rallied solidly a week before its earnings are due, traders said.
By around 1400 CST/2000 GMT, Iomega shares were up 1-3/8 at 18-5/8 on consolidated volume of about 7.7 million shares. The stock reached an intraday high of 19-3/8.
Iomega shares began the week at around 16-1/2.
Traders said earnings expectations appeared to be driving the action in the stock and the options.
"It's probably earnings," one trader at the Pacific Stock Exchange said of the increased options activity.
Iomega options trade on four of the five U.S. options exchanges, with the bulk of the order flow going through the American Stock Exchange (AMEX).
On the AMEX, the Iomega February 20 call was the second most active option behind the H&R Block Inc February 30 call, which traded a heavy 8,180 contracts.
The Iomega February 20 had volume of about 5,605. With the stock up, the option added 5/8 to 1-1/4.
That option traded a total of nearly 8,300 contracts. Its open interest through Monday, which included an addition of 2,292 contracts, was 17,482 contracts.
Most of the activity was in the calls, but heavy order flows were seen in the February 15 and 17-1/2 puts also.
"There's been two-sided paper, but most of it on the buy side," one trader said, adding that the February 17-1/2 and 20 calls were the most sought-after options.
He added that some investors and traders who bought the options in the morning were selling in the afternoon to take a quick profit.
"People are receptive to selling to get rid of some of the (options) before the earnings just in case they're flat," the trader said.
Iomega earnings are scheduled to be released on January 28 after the market closes.
Volatilities in the February series were up about 10 points since Friday, traders said.
"Volatilities were down underneath 80 but they popped back up to around 85," one said. "That's about as cheap as it gets.
"We've had it as high as 100, 110, but I don't think we're going to see that again with the New York listing," he said.
In November last year, Iomega shares moved from the Nasdaq stock market to a listing on the New York Stock Exchange.
